name: LTC2850CMS8#PBF
title: LTC2850/LTC2851/LTC2852: 3.3 V 20 Mbps RS485/RS422 transceivers
summary: A family of low power RS485/RS422 transceivers for a 3 V to 3.6 V supply, rated to 20 Mbps. The LTC2850 is half duplex, the LTC2851 full duplex without enables, and the LTC2852 full duplex with enables. Receivers are 1/8 unit load (256 nodes) on C and I grades and hold RO high on an open, shorted or idle bus across -7 V to 12 V. Drivers are current limited, the parts shut down thermally, the bus pins take ±15 kV HBM, and the LTC2850 and LTC2852 drop to 5 µA max in shutdown.
key_figures: |VOD| 1.5 V min into 27 Ω (VCC = 3 V), 2 V min into 50 Ω (VCC = 3.13 V)
96 kΩ min (C, I), 48 kΩ min (H); 125 kΩ typ
driver 10 ns typ, 50 ns max; receiver 50 ns typ, 70 ns max
370 µA typ receive, 450 µA typ transmit; shutdown 5 µA max (C, I)
±15 kV HBM on A, B, Y, Z
C 0 °C to 70 °C; I -40 °C to 85 °C; H -40 °C to 125 °C

notes: An order code reads: part number, temperature grade, package code, then #PBF (lead free) or #TRPBF (lead free, tape and reel). Grades: C, 0 °C to 70 °C; I, -40 °C to 85 °C; H, -40 °C to 125 °C. Package codes: DD, 8-lead or 10-lead plastic DFN; MS8, 8-lead plastic MSOP; MS, 10-lead plastic MSOP; S8, 8-lead plastic SO; S, 14-lead plastic SO. LTC2850CMS8#PBF is the LTC2850, commercial grade, 8-lead MSOP, lead free.

circuits.title: Typical application: two LTC2850 on one terminated twisted pair
circuits.description: Two half-duplex LTC2850 nodes share one twisted pair. A ties to A and B ties to B, and a termination resistor RT spans the pair at each end. Each node has its own supply and ground (VCC1/GND1, VCC2/GND2), and its RO, RE, DE and DI pins are the logic connections to that node's controller.
notes: GND1 and GND2 are the separate grounds of the two nodes.
BUS_A and BUS_B are the two wires of one twisted pair.

circuits.title: Failsafe "0" application (idle state = logic "0")
circuits.description: An LTC2850 whose bus pins are crossed onto the cable: pin B goes to the line marked "A" and pin A to the line marked "B". An inverter I1 sits between the transceiver's RO pin and the RO logic line, with a 100k pull-up from the RO pin to VCC, and an inverter I2 sits between the DI logic line and the DI pin. With the two inversions and the crossed pair, an idle bus reads as logic 0 on the RO line.
notes: RE and DE are open logic leads.

circuits.title: Multi-node network with end termination using the LTC2850 and LTC2854
circuits.description: A half-duplex bus on one twisted pair. An LTC2854 sits at each end of the cable with its TE pin at 3.3 V, which switches in the 120 Ω termination built into that part across its A and B pins. Two LTC2850 nodes tap the pair between the ends, A to A and B to B. Every node's RO, RE, DE and DI are open logic leads.
notes: The two TE leads are each tied to 3.3 V.

circuits.title: Full duplex network using the LTC2852 and LTC2855
circuits.description: A four-node full-duplex bus on two twisted pairs. The master, an LTC2855 at the left end, drives one pair from Y and Z and listens on the other through A and B, with TE at 3.3 V switching its own termination across A and B. Two LTC2852 slaves tap both pairs: their A and B take the master's driven pair and their Y and Z drive the master's listening pair. At the right end a slave LTC2855 drives the listening pair, which is ended there by a 120 Ω resistor, and receives the master's pair with its own termination switched in by TE at 3.3 V.

parts.note: across the slave-to-master pair at the right end

notes: MS_P/MS_N is the master-to-slave pair and SM_P/SM_N the slave-to-master pair.

operation.text: Three 3.3 V RS485/RS422 transceivers rated to 20 Mbps. The LTC2850 is half duplex: driver and receiver share the A/B pair, with DE and RE enables and a low power shutdown. The LTC2851 is full duplex (driver on Y/Z, receiver on A/B) with neither enable and no shutdown, in 8 leads. The LTC2852 is full duplex with both enables and shutdown, in 10 or 14 leads. Each comes in C (0 °C to 70 °C), I (-40 °C to 85 °C) and H (-40 °C to 125 °C) grades.

With the driver on and DI high, Y-Z is positive on the LTC2851 and LTC2852 and A-B is positive on the LTC2850. With it off both outputs go high impedance. On the full-duplex parts the leakage of Y and Z stays below 10 µA from -7 V to 12 V; on the LTC2850 A and B, when off, look like the receiver's own input resistance, RIN. The driver outputs stay free of glitches while the supply rises or falls.

The driver outputs survive a short to anything between VCC - 15 V and 15 V, the absolute maximum span; such a short peaks at typically no more than 180 mA. When a high output is pulled a little above VCC, current flows back into the supply; the driver keeps conducting until the output is about 1.4 V over VCC and then shuts this reverse current off, so a receiver load with a positive common mode still works. The reverse peak can reach 300 mA in the cold; where the supply cannot sink it, a 3.6 V zener across the supply takes it.

Every part turns off both its driver and its receiver when it overheats; the protection trips when the junction exceeds 150 °C (Note 4). Current limiting on all outputs plus this shutdown keep bus contention or a fault from dissipating too much power.

When the receiver is on and |A-B| exceeds 200 mV, RO follows the sign of A-B. RO is held high when the inputs are open, shorted together, or terminated with nothing driving them, anywhere in the -7 V to 12 V common-mode range. RO is driven actively to VCC or ground and needs no pull-up. With the receiver off RO is high impedance, leaking under ±1 µA inside the supply range.

On C and I grades each bus input is above 96 kΩ to ground, eight times the RS485 unit load, so a part is 1/8 unit load and up to 256 of them fit on one line within the standard. H-grade inputs are above 48 kΩ, a 1/4 unit load. The input resistance holds whether the receiver is on or off and the part powered or not.

On the LTC2850 and LTC2852, RE high with DE low puts the part in a low power shutdown that draws 5 µA at most (C and I grades, 15 µA for H). Entering shutdown takes up to 100 ns after the enable edge (tSHDN), and the driver or receiver comes back within 8 µs of being enabled from shutdown.

Unloaded, the parts draw typically under 500 µA in any mode. Once the cable is terminated the driver load dominates the supply current: two 120 Ω terminations and a 2 V differential output give 33 mA of DC load current, supplied from VCC. Toggling data adds current that charges the load capacitance, a term that grows steeply at high data rates (Figure 13).
VCC runs from 3 V to 3.6 V and takes a 0.1 µF ceramic decoupling capacitor.
The bus pins (A, B, Y, Z) withstand ±15 kV human body model without latchup or damage.

Use a ground plane, and place a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor within a quarter inch of the VCC pin. Keep the A/B and Y/Z traces short and matched. Space the two lines of a differential pair more than one trace width apart, and do not stack them over one another on different layers. Route the outputs away from sensitive inputs; on the full-duplex parts keep DI and A/B away from the driver and receiver outputs, since coupling can cause noise, jitter or oscillation.

The logic inputs have 150 mV of hysteresis about a threshold of typically 1.5 V. Driver edges disturb ground and supply, more so with capacitive load, and an input held near its threshold can then change state. Hold the inputs at proper logic levels and pass through the threshold faster than 1 V/µs; good decoupling and correct termination also reduce these glitches.

How far a signal travels at a given rate depends on the cable (Figure 14). At low rates the limit is the cable's resistance, so the length is flat; above that, AC losses make the length fall as the rate rises. The RS485/RS422 standard stops at 10 Mbps; these parts go to 20 Mbps.
